## Rule

Input is a same-size binary shape using colors `0` and `5`. The color-5
foreground decomposes uniquely into non-overlapping pieces:

- `2x2` square tetrominoes become output color `8`.
- Straight length-3 horizontal/vertical bars become output color `2`.
- Background remains `0`.

The public/train/test/arc-gen set is consistent with a unique exact cover by
those two piece types.

**The hidden-correctness cliff sits between 92.86% and 95.65% truth.** The 3823
ship (92.86%) lost the entire +16.58; LIVE (95.65%) keeps it. ~2.8 pp of
truth-corpus accuracy is the entire margin between +16.58 and −16.58.
Cheaper-via-fewer-hidden-channels always falls off this cliff (q-h3 4347→89.9%).

**Lossless-compression floor reached:** `polish_candidate.py` on LIVE finds 0

**Verdict: no-candidate.** Cheaper-and-safe requires either (a) a lossless

## Algorithm sketch

Reference oracle:

1. Build all foreground-supported `2x2` square candidates.
2. Enumerate non-overlapping square subsets.
3. For each subset, remove those square cells from the foreground.
4. Accept the subset only if the residual can be recursively partitioned into
   straight length-3 bars.
5. The unique accepted square subset marks color `8`; the remaining foreground
   marks color `2`.

`task023/prototypes/build_task023_structural_v1.py` contains this numpy oracle
and verifies it at `266/266` before building the ONNX.

`task023/prototypes/build_task023_exactcover_v2.py` compiles the same idea into
ONNX without learned weights: branch on the lexicographically first remaining
foreground cell; try only the three possible pieces starting there (`2x2`
square, horizontal length-3 bar, vertical length-3 bar); collect completed
states across a seven-step unroll by foreground area.

## Don't-do log

- Do not use the current `submissions/submission.zip` task023 artifact as the
  canonical baseline for this work; it contains a cherry13b/identity-style probe
  stub. Use `submissions/_canonical_6166_58_backup.zip` when comparing canonical
  task023 behavior/cost.
- Do not ship `task023_structural_v1.onnx` as-is. It is public-perfect but fails
  the hard synth gate at `636/1000`, exactly the visible-fit shortcut trap for
  cherry13b-zero tasks.
- Do not trust canonical-equivalent crop/compression as a hidden unlock. The
  canonical/crop model also scores only `226/1000` against the exact-cover synth
  oracle.
- Do not repeat the unpruned exhaustive all-configuration lookup/count path in a
  blunt form; the naive enumeration timed out. If revived, prune by known square
  count (`area mod 3`) and bit-pack aggressively.
- Do not retry "collect only complete-count prefixes"; the first patch looked
  plausible but dropped synth to `664/1000` because synth includes covers like
  `2S+4B` (area 20), which are complete at depth 6 even though they are only
  prefixes of the `3S+4B` legal-pruning family. Task-shaped area collection
  must include the synth-only `3S+2B` and `2S+4B` areas, not only the named
  public piece-count families.
- Do not switch square-mask branch state to compact square-origin slots using
  per-collection reconstruction for every candidate row. That earlier obvious
  version stayed correct but worsened score to `1,022,698`; the working version
  reconstructs only the selected valid row.
- Do not use variable-`K` dynamic compaction. A dynamic `TopK` version was
  correct but the official scorer returned `memory=None` because strict shape
  inference rejects symbolic dimensions. Use fixed caps if compacting branches.
- Do not carry a row-occupancy mask as explicit branch state. The measured
  version stayed correct but worsened rowpack-v3 from `152,557` to `163,628`.
- Do not tighten v5 caps to `3,8,18,28,32,24`: visible and 1k synth pass, but
  broad synth misses valid square sets (`4999/5000` at `seed=24023`,
  `19998/20000` at `seed=25023`).
- Do not ship `task023_origin_top3_v1/v2` as exact-safe. They prove sub-20k is
  possible for a public-perfect learned ranker, but they miss about `1.5-2%`
  of broad exact-cover synth grids.
- Do not assume "more hidden channels" improves the learned ranker: H72
  QLinearConv stayed under 20k but did not beat H30+chooser on synth.
- Do not use the top-6 chooser for the under-20 target: it scores `20,738` and
  did not clearly improve the broad seed checked.
- Do not use top-6 dynamic chooser for the under-15 target: row/col overlap
  checks get it down to `15,744`, still over cap.
- Do not use H24 top-4 chooser for the under-10 target: it scores `11,608`,
  despite improving the 1k synth smoke gate.
- Do not treat the under-5 tiny rankers as exact-safe structural solves. The
  best under-5 H4 model is public-perfect and much cheaper, but still misses
  broad exact-cover synth.
- Do not remove the support gate from the tiny rankers: unsupported origins
  saturate to high scores and visible accuracy collapses.
- Do not feed `UINT8` scores directly to `TopK`; ONNX checker/simplifier accept
  it, but ORT load fails with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` for `TopK(11)`. Keep the
  `UINT8 -> F16` cast before `TopK`.
- Do not single-scatter optional third-square cells with false updates directly:
  if predicted square cells overlap, false third updates can overwrite true
  top-2 cells. The working single-scatter variant gates disabled third cells to
  a repeated top-2 cell and uses all-true updates.
- Do not ship `task023_direct_dynidx_3918.onnx` unless the risk profile is
  intentionally changed; it is visible-perfect but fails the ≥91% synth guard.
- Do not emit BOOL output under opset 11; ONNX Runtime rejects BOOL `Pad`.
- Do not replace the per-piece fit check with `ReduceMin` directly on UINT8;
  ONNX Runtime rejects UINT8 `ReduceMin` in opset 11.
